title: Struct assignment, comparison limitations and serialization cautions (CodeSaathi extension)
learningObjectives: Assign compatible structure objects using the assignment operator.
Explain why C does not provide built-in whole-structure equality comparison.
Compare members explicitly according to application semantics.
Explain why memcmp is not a general semantic structure comparison.
Avoid serializing raw structure bytes as a portable interchange format.

understand.concept: Structure assignment copies the value of each member from one compatible structure object to another. C does not provide a built-in == operator for comparing complete structure values. Padding and pointer members also complicate raw byte comparison and serialization.
understand.whyItMatters: A correct comparison should express which fields define equality. A portable serialized form should encode each field with specified widths, ordering and representation.
understand.analogy: Treat each object or stream as a resource with a defined lifetime and explicit rules for access.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's formal object, storage-duration, alignment or library rules.

explain.narrative:
Structure assignment copies the value of each member from one compatible structure object to another. C does not provide a built-in == operator for comparing complete structure values. Padding and pointer members also complicate raw byte comparison and serialization.

Check all allocation, I/O and conversion results. Respect object bounds and lifetime, initialize data before reading it, and define who owns and releases each resource.

examples.title: Assign and compare structure members
examples.explanation: Structure assignment copies member values. The comparison function expresses the application's semantic equality by comparing both fields.

examples.title: Compare pointed-to content deliberately
examples.explanation: A structure containing a pointer needs an explicit comparison contract. This function compares the pointed-to byte sequences, not just pointer addresses; callers must ensure both ranges are valid for their stated lengths.

practise.guidedTask: Implement a structure assignment example and a comparison function that checks the fields relevant to the application's meaning.
practise.independentTask: Design a structure containing a pointer and length. Define whether equality means pointer identity or equal pointed-to contents, implement that rule, and explain why raw memcmp is not a substitute.
hints: Structure assignment copies member values, including pointer values.
C does not define == for whole structures.
Padding can make memcmp unsuitable for semantic equality.
Choose explicitly whether pointer identity or pointed-to content matters.
Use a field-by-field comparison or a defined serialization format.

questions.answer: The pointer value is copied, not the pointed-to object
questions.explanation: Structure assignment is not a deep copy of pointed-to storage.
